newsitem.title: BELGIUM: INSIGHT - Bel-20 seen unable to set new highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bel-20 seen unable to set new highs.

text.p: Belgian shares are expected to get some support this week from the Bundesbank's rate cut last Thursday, but chartists do not expect the Bel-20 index of leading shares to break above the all-time high set in May.
Most chartists predict a period of consolidation before further trends emerge. Low volumes because of the summer holidays are also affecting the pattern.
The Bel-20 ended at 1,767.53 last week, up from its August 16 close of 1751.32. On Friday, the index came close to its all-time high in early trade, but failed to confirm this at the close.
(Please note: contributions have been affected by summer holidays)

CERA - A cut in German interest rates last Thursday sent bond yields lower and the Bel-20 index above the former resistance of 1,750 (this is now our first support level). In July, Belgian business confidence rose further, confirming signs of a recovery that began at the start of the year. A first resistance is at the last closing high of 1,773 (on May 28). A second is at the psychologically important level of 1,800. Last week the Bel-20 reached an intra-day high of 1,776.46 (on the opening of August 23) but fell back below 1,770. The Bel-20 could rise further in the coming days, led by cyclical stocks, amid evidence the economy is growing. -- Guy Sips.

ECOFIS - The Bel-20 took its two resistance levels last week, coming close to its 1,781-point all-time high reached in May. We do not expect that this all-time high will be taken easily. The weekly stochastics show an overbought picture, and the Dow shows a spinning top in the weekly candle chart. We consider the strong upmove of last week as part of an extended top formation. Next week the Bel-20 is likely to move sideways to down. -- Frank Boll.

Generale Bank - Resistance levels gave way at last after the surprise move by the Bundesbank. Although the short-term trend is still positive, the technical picture calls for caution. The swift upsurge was established on relatively low volume and needs confirmation. A further rise would be a very bullish signal, but the market looks too weak for the moment to consider this a serious possibility. If the Bel-20 index drops back into the 1,745-1,755 range (that was in place for the last two weeks) a further correction is likely -- with a first target at 1,730. The longer-term uptrend remains in place as long as 1,580 holds. -- Geert Vanderbeke.
